findings.cross_file_justification: endpoint_policy.validate_providers accepts provider-level dispatch_group: local, and hop_is_local inherits that label for models. The adapter checks only the model-level field.
findings.description: An authenticated provider declaring dispatch_group: local with an HTTPS loopback endpoint, no insecure opt-in, and no model-level dispatch_group passes validation and is classified as local, but receives no TransportPolicy.
findings.failure_mode: Requests use environment proxies, allowing prompts and credentials intended for a local endpoint to pass through a configured proxy, violating the local transport guarantee.
findings.suggested_fix: Resolve provider-level dispatch_group inheritance when constructing ModelConfig, and apply TransportPolicy to every hop classified as local.

findings.cross_file_justification: The loader calls validate_providers, but that function does not call the separately defined endpoint_policy.validate_local_fallbacks.
findings.description: The local_voices fallback restriction is never enforced by the added configuration validation. A local model can declare a fallback_chain pointing to a hosted provider and still load successfully.
findings.failure_mode: When the local hop fails and cheval walks its fallback chain, the prompt can reach a hosted provider despite hounfour.locality: local_voices.
findings.suggested_fix: Invoke validate_local_fallbacks on the merged configuration after provider validation and before returning it from load_config.

findings.cross_file_justification: endpoint_policy.hop_is_local (and validate_local_fallbacks / the planner mirror hop-locality.py) treat a provider-block `dispatch_group: local` as labelling every silent model entry local. The diff-touched readers in cheval.py (_build_provider_config), openai_adapter.py (_transport_policy, health_check) and modelinv.py (hop_locality_of) read only the model-level key.
findings.description: ModelConfig.dispatch_group is populated solely from model_data.get("dispatch_group"). A provider whose block says `dispatch_group: local` with silent model entries is admitted by validate_providers (_local_labels honours the block) and classified local by hop_is_local / the planner under `locality: local_voices`, yet: (a) OpenAIAdapter._transport_policy sees dispatch_group None and, absent allow_insecure_endpoint (an https local host needs none), runs the hop with no TransportPolicy — proxy env honoured, urllib fallback follows redirects; (b) modelinv.hop_locality_of records hop_locality="hosted" for the same hop; (c) health_check applies the policy only for allow_insecure_endpoint, never for a local dispatch_group. Three diverging definitions of 'local' for one hop.
findings.failure_mode: Under local_voices the planner believes a hop is local while the adapter sends it without the D-7.2 request-time rules and MODELINV records it as hosted; a redirecting or proxied local https endpoint could move the prompt off the declared host with no telemetry trace.
findings.suggested_fix: Resolve dispatch_group once (model entry, else provider block) in _build_provider_config and pass it to ModelConfig; have modelinv.hop_locality_of delegate to endpoint_policy.hop_is_local; apply TransportPolicy in health_check when the provider is local by that rule, not only when opted in.

findings.cross_file_justification: ledger.py now writes a third priced value `stale_catalog` into `pricing_source`. rollup.py was updated to count it as priced, but the module docstring names cost-report.sh as a second direct reader of the ledger ("cost-report.sh counts long_context_rows"), and that script is not in the change set.
findings.description: A new ledger enum value was introduced without updating every reader. cost-report.sh (jq over the JSONL) is documented as a ledger consumer and is absent from the diff and from the truncated file list; any `pricing_source == "config"` test there will classify stale_catalog rows as unpriced, diverging from rollup.py.
findings.failure_mode: Once any catalog entry carries a price_date older than 90 days, cost reports from the shell path show those calls as unpriced / cost-unknown while rollup.py counts them as priced — two reports disagree on the same ledger.
findings.suggested_fix: Grep all ledger readers (cost-report.sh, any dashboards) for `pricing_source` and accept `stale_catalog` alongside `config`; add a test that enumerates allowed values in one place.

findings.description: The final emit derives the hop for destination/hop_locality from `final_model_id`, else `models_failed[-1]["model"]`, else `models_requested[0]`. The models_failed dicts store `model` and `provider` as separate keys (see the context_window hunk: `"model": _entry_target, "provider": _entry.provider`), so `model` is very likely a bare model id with no `:`; `hop_telemetry` then silently returns only locality_mode. The same applies if `models_requested[0]` is an alias.
findings.failure_mode: For an all-hops-failed invocation (the case where destination matters most for forensics) the MODELINV row omits `destination` and `hop_locality`, contradicting the FR-7/FR-8 comment 'every MODELINV row carries destination + locality' with no warning.
findings.suggested_fix: Build the hop as f"{failed['provider']}:{failed['model']}" from the models_failed entry, and resolve aliases in models_requested through the planner before calling hop_telemetry; log when hop_telemetry cannot derive a destination for a non-empty hop.

findings.description: TransportPolicy is constructed and threaded through http_post / http_get / http_post_stream only by OpenAIAdapter. ProviderConfig.allow_insecure_endpoint and the loader's validation are provider-type agnostic, so an opted-in provider of any other adapter type (e.g. an anthropic-type block pointing at http://127.0.0.1) passes load but its adapter calls http_post without `policy`, so proxy env vars are honoured and the urllib fallback follows redirects.
findings.failure_mode: The module docstring's request-time guarantee ('for an opted-in provider ... the adapter ignores proxy environment variables, refuses HTTP redirects') is only true for openai/openai_compat; other opted-in providers get load-time checks only.
findings.suggested_fix: Either refuse allow_insecure_endpoint / dispatch_group local at load for provider types whose adapter does not implement TransportPolicy, or move policy construction into ProviderAdapter base so every adapter's transport calls receive it.

findings.description: validate_providers passes the raw interpolated `endpoint` to validate_declared_endpoint. Catalog endpoints with a `{region}` placeholder exist (modelinv.destination_for explicitly substitutes `region_default` into `{region}` before split_url), but validate_providers performs no such substitution. If the canonical validator's host grammar rejects `{`/`}` (as a strict hostname regex would), load_config fails for every configuration that includes such a provider, regardless of whether it is used.
findings.failure_mode: A single templated-endpoint provider in the merged catalog turns every cheval invocation into a ConfigError at load; the failure is global, not scoped to the hop.
findings.suggested_fix: Substitute region_default into `{region}` (or skip/relax the host check for templated endpoints) in validate_providers, mirroring destination_for, and add a test_config_examples_load case with a `{region}` endpoint.
